question.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨3,0,-4⟩,\,{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨0,3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5})\cdot q(t)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{5}\cdot q(t)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{5}\cdot q(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{5}\cdot {q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{3}{5}⟨0,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{3}{5}⟨0,1,0⟩}{(\frac{3}{5})} \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{5}q(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot ⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨3,0,-4⟩\cdot ⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\cdot 0+0\cdot 1-4\cdot 0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
